record.original_question: Does every minimal forbidden subgraph for torus embeddability have fewer than 100 edges?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4 Does every minimal forbidden subgraph for the torus have fewer than 100 edges?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is said to embed in the torus if it can be drawn on the torus (the closed orientable surface of genus 1) without edge crossings. A graph $G$ is called a minimal forbidden subgraph for torus embeddability (a torus obstruction in the topological-minor sense) if $G$ does not embed in the torus, but every proper subgraph of $G$ obtained by deleting a single edge or contracting/suppressing a degree-2 vertex does embed in the torus; equivalently, $G$ is minor-minimal (or topological-minor-minimal) with respect to non-embeddability in the torus. By the Robertson–Seymour theorem, the set of such minimal obstructions is finite.

Question: Does every minimal forbidden subgraph for torus embeddability have fewer than 100 edges?
artifact.status_search_result: The complete set of minimal torus obstructions is still unknown. Computational searches have found at least tens of thousands of obstructions, but no proven upper bound on the number of edges in a minimal torus obstruction has been established. The 100-edge bound conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Large Set of Torus Obstructions and How They Were Discovered
status_evidence.snippet: Exhaustive searches have discovered hundreds of thousands of torus obstructions, but the complete list is not known.
status_evidence.claim: The full set of minimal torus obstructions is not yet determined, so the edge-size question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Toroidal graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: By Robertson–Seymour the set of minimal non-toroidal graphs is finite, but it has at least 17,523 graphs and the complete set is unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The minimal obstruction set for the torus is finite but not fully characterized.
